html:
On the 1000 and 1100 maps, Pratiharas labels the middle Ganges plain, where the once great Gurjara-Pratihara empire had shrunk to a small kingdom around Kannauj, and where its heirs then ruled. The shape also stretches east toward Bihar and the Nepal hills.

By 1000 the Pratiharas had lost their outer provinces to former vassals such as the Chandelas and the Kalachuris. In 1018 Mahmud of Ghazni marched on Kannauj, and the Pratihara king fled. The dynasty died out a few decades later.

Around 1090 a new family, the Gahadavalas, took Kannauj and Varanasi and ruled the plain through the 1100s. Their last great king, Jayachandra, was killed fighting Muhammad of Ghor at the Battle of Chandawar in 1194, which opened the Ganges plain to the new Delhi Sultanate.
